steps: Do not download or open the file.
If you installed it, switch off mobile data and Wi-Fi, then uninstall the app.
Open Settings and remove any app you don't recognise from Accessibility and device-admin access, then run a Google Play Protect scan.
From a different device, change your banking and email passwords, and ask your bank to block your cards if a banking app was on this phone.
If money has left your account, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
apk_malware_link.summary: The message asks you to install an app from a link instead of the Play Store. Such apps can read your SMS and OTPs and take over your phone.
apk_malware_link.title: App-install (APK) scam

steps: Do not open or install the file, and delete it from the chat.
If you installed it, switch off mobile data and Wi-Fi, then uninstall the app.
Open Settings and remove any app you don't recognise from Accessibility and device-admin access, then run a Google Play Protect scan.
Call the person it came from: their WhatsApp may be hacked and sending the file to all their contacts.
If money has left your account, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
app_file.summary: The file is an app or a program, not a document or a photo. Once installed, such apps read your SMS and OTPs and empty bank accounts; fake wedding invitations, challans and KYC forms are sent this way.
app_file.title: App or program sent as a file

steps: Do not tap the link or call any number given in the message.
Never share your OTP, PIN, CVV or password. Banks never ask for these by SMS, call or link.
If you already entered details, open your bank's official app or call the number printed on the back of your card, and block net banking and your cards.
If money has left your account, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
Report the message on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu) at sancharsaathi.gov.in, then delete it.
bank_kyc_scam.summary: Someone is pretending to be your bank and saying your account will be blocked unless you "update KYC" through their link or number.
bank_kyc_scam.title: Fake bank KYC (Know Your Customer) message

steps: If the target is your device, make sure it uses a long, unique password, and turn off password login where you can (use keys or one-time codes).
Disconnect the device doing the guessing if it is on your Wi-Fi.
Change the passwords of any account on the targeted service.
brute_force.summary: A device is trying to log in again and again in a short time. Someone is guessing passwords.
brute_force.title: Password guessing

steps: Do not pay through the link, however small the amount.
Check the parcel yourself in the courier's official app or website, opened by you, using your real tracking number.
If you entered card details, block the card through your bank's official app or the number on the card.
If money has left your account, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
Report the message on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu) at sancharsaathi.gov.in.
delivery_fee_scam.summary: The message says a parcel is stuck or needs a small fee. The link leads to a fake page that steals card details.
delivery_fee_scam.title: Fake parcel or delivery fee

steps: Think whether something changed (a new app, an update, a new use). If not, disconnect the device until it is checked.
Update the device; reset IoT devices to factory settings if the alert repeats.
Watch for more alerts about the same device.
device_anomaly.summary: A device suddenly sent much more traffic than usual and talked to many servers it never used before. That can be an update, or a sign that it was taken over.
device_anomaly.title: Device behaving unlike its normal self

steps: Disconnect the device from the Wi-Fi.
Run a full security scan; if it is an IoT device or the scan finds nothing, reset it to factory settings.
From a different, clean device, change the passwords of accounts used on the infected one.
dga_domains.summary: A device looked up many random-looking website names in a few minutes. Malware does this to find its controller's current address.
dga_domains.title: Malware looking for its controller (random website names)

steps: Hang up. Do not stay on video calls, and do not transfer any money.
Tell a family member or friend immediately; scammers rely on keeping you isolated and scared.
If you are worried about a real case, contact your local police station yourself, using a number you look up.
If you already paid, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
Report the call or message on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu) at sancharsaathi.gov.in.
digital_arrest_scam.summary: Someone claims to be from the police, CBI, customs or a court and threatens arrest unless you pay or stay on a video call. Real officials never arrest you or demand money over a call.
digital_arrest_scam.title: "Digital arrest" or fake police threat

steps: Disconnect the device from the Wi-Fi.
Run a full security scan, or reset an IoT device to factory settings.
From a different, clean device, change the passwords of accounts used on the affected one.
dns_tunnel.summary: A device made many long, never-repeating lookups under one website. Malware uses DNS like this to sneak data out or to take orders past security checks.
dns_tunnel.title: Data hidden in DNS lookups

steps: Find the device in the alert and disconnect it from the Wi-Fi.
If it is an IoT device, reset it to factory settings and update it before reconnecting.
If your own device or service is the target, restart it and keep an eye on the alerts.
dos_flood.summary: A device is sending a flood of connections to one target, to overload it so that it stops working.
dos_flood.title: Flood of traffic (denial of service)

steps: Do not tap links, call numbers or install anything from this message.
Never share an OTP, PIN, CVV or password.
If it claims to be from a company or bank, contact them yourself through their official app or website.
If money has left your account, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
Report the message on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu) at sancharsaathi.gov.in.
generic_suspicious.summary: The message shows warning signs of a scam, even though it does not match one known pattern exactly.
generic_suspicious.title: Suspicious message

steps: Do not open the file, and delete it from the chat.
If you opened it, do not click "Enable content", "Enable macros" or "Allow".
If you clicked one of those, disconnect the device from the internet and run a malware scan: Google Play Protect on a phone, Windows Security on a computer.
From another device, change the passwords you used on that device.
If money has left your account, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
harmful_document.summary: The document carries hidden code, macros or a command that runs when it is opened or allowed. This is how malware gets onto phones and computers.
harmful_document.title: Document with hidden code

steps: Do not pay any registration, training or deposit money to get a job or tasks.
Do not join the groups or apps the message points to, and do not share ID documents.
Check the company yourself through its official website, not the link sent to you.
If money has left your account, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
Report the message on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu) at sancharsaathi.gov.in.
job_task_scam.summary: The message offers easy work or daily earnings but soon asks you to pay a fee or deposit money to "unlock" tasks or earnings.
job_task_scam.title: Job or "task" scam

steps: Do not pay any "processing", "tax" or "registration" fee, and do not share bank details or OTPs.
Do not tap the link. Income-tax refunds go straight to your pre-validated bank account; you never claim them through a link.
If you already paid or shared details, contact your bank through its official app or the number on your card.
If money has left your account, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
Report the message on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu) at sancharsaathi.gov.in.
lottery_reward_scam.summary: The message promises a prize, cashback or refund but needs a fee, your bank details or an OTP first. Genuine prizes and refunds never ask for these.
lottery_reward_scam.title: Prize, lottery or refund scam

steps: Check the device in the alert: uninstall apps you do not recognise and run a security scan (Play Protect on Android, Windows Security on a PC).
If it is an IoT device, update its software, and reset it to factory settings if the alert repeats.
If you cannot explain the traffic, disconnect the device until it is checked.
malware_beacon.summary: A device keeps contacting the same unknown server at an exact rhythm. Malware checks in with its controller this way.
malware_beacon.title: Device calling home at fixed times (possible malware)

steps: Unplug the device or remove it from the Wi-Fi now.
Reset it to factory settings, update its software, and change its default password before you connect it again.
Check the other devices on your network for the same alert.
network_scan.summary: A device is trying to reach many machines on the same port. Infected cameras, routers and other IoT devices do this to spread malware.
network_scan.title: Device scanning other machines (worm or botnet)

steps: Do not share the OTP, PIN, CVV or password with anyone, even someone claiming to be from a bank, company or government office.
Read the OTP message itself: it says what the code is for. If you did not start that action, someone else is trying.
If you already shared it, contact your bank through its official app or the number on your card and block the account or card.
If money has left your account, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
otp_theft.summary: The message tries to get your one-time password, PIN or card details, which would let someone empty your account or take over your apps.
otp_theft.title: OTP or password theft

steps: Do not click the links in the document, and do not type anything into it.
If you typed a password, PIN or card number, change it at once in the official app or website, and call your bank to block the card.
Never share an OTP, whoever asks for it.
Delete the file and block the sender.
If money has left your account, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
phishing_document.summary: The document leads to a fake website, or is itself a fake sign-in page. Whatever you type there goes to the scammer.
phishing_document.title: Document that leads to a fake website

steps: Do not open the link. If you opened it, close the page without typing anything.
If you typed a password, PIN or card number there, change that password at once from the official app, and call your bank to block the card.
To check your account or an offer, open the official app or type the website address yourself.
If money has left your account, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
Report the message on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu) at sancharsaathi.gov.in.
phishing_link.summary: The link leads to a website that is likely fake: it is made to look like a real company or office so that you type your password, card details or OTP into it.
phishing_link.title: Fake website link (phishing)

steps: On that device, close the website without typing anything.
If a password, PIN, OTP or card number was typed there, change that password at once from the official app and call your bank to block the card.
Find the message or app that opened the link and delete it.
If money has left your account, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
phishing_lookup.summary: A device on your network looked up a website that is on the public list of phishing sites, or that copies a bank or brand. Someone may be about to type a password, card number or OTP into a fake page.
phishing_lookup.title: Device opened a phishing website

steps: Find the device in the alert (its name or address). If you do not recognise it, change the Wi-Fi password so it is thrown off.
If it is your own device, disconnect it from the Wi-Fi, update it, and reset it to factory settings if the alert repeats.
Turn off remote-login services you do not use (Telnet, SSH, remote desktop) on your devices.
port_scan.summary: A device is trying many ports on another device, one after another. Attackers do this to find a way in, and infected devices do it to spread.
port_scan.title: Port scan on your network

steps: Ignore it; replying can confirm that your number is active.
Do not tap links in unexpected offers; open the brand's official app instead.
Turn on Do Not Disturb for promotional messages through your mobile operator's app or by contacting 1909.
promo_spam.summary: This looks like unwanted marketing rather than a scam. It is annoying but usually not dangerous.
promo_spam.title: Promotional spam

steps: Find the device in the alert and check which apps or services it runs.
If it is an IoT device, update it and change its default password; reset it if the alert repeats.
Uninstall apps you do not recognise, and run a security scan on phones and computers.
risky_port.summary: A device connected to the internet on a port home devices never use, such as Telnet or IRC. Malware uses these to spread or to take orders.
risky_port.title: Connection on a port malware uses

steps: On that device, close the page without typing anything.
If a password, PIN, OTP or card number was typed there, change that password at once from the official app and call your bank to block the card.
Delete the message and block its sender.
If money has left your account, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
scam_link_opened.summary: A device on your Wi-Fi opened a website that came in a message the Pi had flagged as a scam. Someone may be about to type a password, card number or OTP into a fake page.
scam_link_opened.title: Link from a scam message opened

steps: Do not call the number or pay through the link.
Check your bill status in your electricity provider's official app or website, or at its office.
Never install apps or "remote support" tools that a caller asks for.
If money has left your account, call 1930 immediately and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
Report the message on Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu) at sancharsaathi.gov.in.
utility_disconnection_scam.summary: The message threatens to cut your electricity or service tonight unless you call a number or pay through a link.
utility_disconnection_scam.title: Fake electricity or bill disconnection

safe.headline: LIKELY SAFE: no red flags found
steps: Stay careful: never share an OTP, PIN or password, whoever asks.
safe.what: We found no warning signs in this message.
safe.why: It does not match the scam patterns we know.
